curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8856-1/ (scans; the helicopter is pages 4-27, steps 1-28, the second model after, and the last pages add the 8720 motor)

functions.does: The big white handwheel on the right side spins the main rotor through a bevel gear at the foot of the rotor mast, and a crown gear on the mast drives the long shaft with universal joints down the tail boom, which spins the tail rotor through a bevel pair at the tail.
functions.source: book: steps 18 (mast with crown gear), 23 (gear on the front of the tail shaft), 24 (handwheel), 26-28 (rotors); cover arrows on both rotors

functions.does: The small crank low on the right side retracts and lowers the landing gear: a worm turns the long shaft under the floor, which swings the nose wheel's leg through a bevel pair at the front and the two main wheels' legs through a crown gear on the rear axle.
functions.source: book: steps 1-7 and 9-11 (the shaft, the bevel pair, the crown gear and the legs; the step 11 underside view), step 14 (worm); that it folds the gear away is inferred from the build and the cover blueprint's arrow at the nose wheel
functions.note: The worm makes it slow: many turns of the crank per swing of the legs. The nose leg's two plates must swing together with their axle p77 3706. Unsure how far the legs swing and whether they fold forward or back.

functions.does: The small crank low on the left side winds the winch: a 16-tooth gear and a bevel pair turn the drum behind the seats, and the rope runs up over the tip of the hoist arm to the hook, which rises or falls.
functions.source: book: steps 14-16 (crank axle, bevel pair and drum with the string), step 24 (crank)

functions.does: The small crank high on the left side swings the black hoist arm, with the hook hanging from its tip, out over the right-hand door and back in: a worm turns a 16-tooth gear, whose axle swings a short crank arm, and a link pushes the hoist arm round its pivot.
functions.source: book: steps 18 and 22 (worm axle, gear and link), steps 23-24 (hoist arm and crank); that it swings the arm out and in is inferred from the linkage

functions.does: Pushing the control stick in the cockpit forward or back tilts the main rotor forward or back: the lever under the stick pulls a flex cable to a bellcrank by the rotor mast, which pushes a black arm up against the rotor's holder.
functions.source: book: steps 4-6 (stick pivot), 12-13 (stick and first cable), 25-26 (bellcrank, arm and rotor holder); cover arrows at the blade tips. Which way of the stick works which cable is inferred from the model
functions.note: Unsure whether the holder p462 2908 stays still while the rotor spins above it on the ball, or turns with it.

functions.does: Pushing the control stick left or right tilts the main rotor sideways: the stick turns the long shaft under the cockpit floor, whose ball arm at the back pulls a second flex cable up the mast to the side of the rotor's holder.
functions.source: book: steps 1-6 (shaft with toggle joints and ball arm), 13 and 16 (stick and second cable), 26 (rotor holder); cover arrows at the blade tips. Which way of the stick works which cable is inferred from the model

functions.does: A pawl rests on the winch crank's 16-tooth gear, so the hook stays where it is wound to.
functions.source: inferred: the submodel is named Winch-Stopper and sits over the winch crank's gear; the book draws no arrow
functions.skip: only resists gravity on the hook; the winch crank works both ways without it

functions.does: The three landing gear wheels roll freely.

questions.question: Which way does the landing gear fold? Does the high left crank swing the hoist arm?
